user: I have a severe peanut allergy, so I avoid any dishes or restaurants that may contain traces of peanuts.
assistant:  I understand your concern about peanut allergy, which is a serious condition that affects many people. It's great that you're taking steps to avoid any traces of peanuts in your food.

When it comes to dining out, it's important to communicate your allergy to the restaurant staff, including the server and the chef, so they can take appropriate precautions to prevent cross-contamination. You can ask if they have a separate area for preparing food for people with allergies, or if they can use fresh utensils and cookware to prepare your meal.

Additionally, you can look for restaurants that specifically cater to people with food allergies or offer allergy-friendly menus. These restaurants often have strict protocols in place to prevent cross-contamination and ensure the safety of their customers with food allergies.

When it comes to packaged or processed foods, be sure to read the label carefully and look for any mention of peanuts or cross-contamination warnings. Even if a product doesn't explicitly list peanuts as an ingredient, it may still contain traces of peanuts due to cross-contamination during the manufacturing process.
